notes: Complete and correct, including suffixed single-file roots and out-of-range offsets; the zip Open special-casing and the squashfs New/NewObject fallback logic are somewhat convoluted, and the tests are extensive.

Works on both backends and handles suffixed roots and offsets past the end, but the fallback lookups in New and NewObject plus the zip Open special-casing are heavier than needed; the escape test only logs the copy error.
The code is identical to the reference fix and adds a reasonable docs section; tests cover squashfs, zip and escape but skip range/seek checks and the zip regular .rclonelink case.

Code is effectively identical to the reference, plus a relevant docs section; the zip unit test is thinner (no range/seek, regular-suffix or single-root checks), though the archive-level tests cover squashfs and the escape case.

Very close to the reference: the suffix is applied before root matching and newObjectNative names entries the same way List does; it is minimal and clean apart from uncommented struct fields, with good zip, squashfs-fixture and escape tests.
A clean, focused implementation that mirrors the reference semantics on both backends, with good table-driven tests including single root, range/seek, regular .rclonelink and an escape check.

Solid on both backends: a newObjectNativeRemote helper keeps lookup, single-file roots and listing consistent, and offsets are clamped; it adds a small defensive sanitize check, with comprehensive tests including copy and escape.

Correct on both backends with offset clamping and a remote-equality check so List and NewObject agree; the newObjectNativeRemote wrapper and extra sanitize check add some complexity, but the tests are comprehensive.

Only zip is handled and squashfs symlinks are still dropped; the skip counter is never logged, the link field is unused, a duplicate skip branch is dead code, children of symlinks are hidden even without --links, and there are no tests.
Zip only, with no squashfs support and no skip notice logged; it silently drops children of symlinks even without --links, adds an unused `link` field, and has no tests.

Adds unrequested hiding of symlink children and name-conflict skipping, plus a refactor; the zip suffix is applied after root matching and suffixed squashfs roots are unsupported, and it diverges from expected behaviour on one hidden test.
Over-engineered: it adds unrequested conflict-skipping and drops members beneath symlinks (which changes what is listed), misses suffixed roots, and failed one hidden test.

Basic behaviour works, but a squashfs root given as the suffixed name gets f.file double-suffixed so the listing comes back empty, zip ignores suffixed roots, and the find closure logic is convoluted.

Zip adds the suffix after root matching, so a root naming the listed `link.rclonelink` isn't recognised, and the squashfs New double-suffixes f.file for a suffixed root; the symlinkOnly find logic is also convoluted.

Main behaviour works in both backends, but the zip suffix is added after root matching and squashfs New ignores suffixed roots, so a single-file root only works under the unsuffixed name; a seek past the end of a squashfs link target errors.
Basic listing and reading work, but single-object roots are broken: zip ignores a suffixed root, the squashfs suffix check in New fails for nested roots, and Open errors on offsets past the end.

Correct for both zip and squashfs: --links gating, a notice naming the flag, suffixed names that List and NewObject agree on, regular .rclonelink members kept as files, suffixed single-file roots, and range/seek on link targets; tests are thorough, including copy and escape checks.

Correct zip and squashfs support: the suffix is added before root matching, a suffixed root resolves correctly, NewObject agrees with List, and the tests are thorough (range/seek, regular .rclonelink, single root, copy, escape).
